titulo: Narrative tenses: past continuous, past perfect, used to
resumen: Past continuous (was/were + -ing) para la acción de fondo que se interrumpe y past simple para la acción corta que la interrumpe: I was cooking dinner when the power went off.
when suele introducir la acción corta y while la larga; during va con un sustantivo, no con una oración: My phone rang during the exam.
Past perfect (had + participio) para lo que ocurrió antes de otro momento pasado, sobre todo con by the time: By the time we got there, the train had left.
Past perfect continuous (had been + -ing) para una actividad que duraba hasta un momento del pasado o que explica cómo estaba alguien: She had been living in London for six years.
used to + infinitivo para hábitos y estados pasados que ya no ocurren; en negativo y pregunta, didn't use to: We used to have a dog. I didn't use to like coffee.

would + infinitivo solo para acciones repetidas, nunca para estados: Every Sunday my grandad would take us to the park, pero no we would have a dog. Para un número concreto de veces, past simple: I went three times.
be used to (estar acostumbrado) y get used to (acostumbrarse) van seguidos de sustantivo o -ing: I'm used to getting up early. I can't get used to driving on the left.
Futuro en el pasado: would para lo que pasaría después y was/were going to para planes que no se cumplieron: She had no idea she would run the company. We were going to go camping, but it rained.

preguntas.q: My phone rang ___ the exam, which was really embarrassing.
preguntas.x: During va seguido de un sustantivo (the exam); while y when necesitan una oración con sujeto y verbo (while I was doing the exam). Meanwhile es un adverbio («mientras tanto») y no puede introducir un sustantivo.

preguntas.q: When I was a child, we ___ a dog called Toby.
preguntas.x: Para un estado pasado que ya no existe se usa used to: we used to have a dog. Would solo vale para acciones repetidas, no para estados como have (poseer), que tampoco va en continuo; en afirmativo se escribe used, con -d.

preguntas.q: I ___ dinner when the power went off, so we ended up eating sandwiches.
preguntas.x: La acción larga que se interrumpe va en past continuous y la que interrumpe en past simple: I was cooking when the power went off. Con cooked o had cooked la cena ya estaría hecha y no habría hecho falta comer sándwiches.

preguntas.q: By the time we got to the station, the train ___.
preguntas.x: By the time + pasado indica que la otra acción ya había terminado antes: the train had left. Con left parecería que el tren salió en ese mismo momento, y has left no encaja en un relato en pasado.

preguntas.q: I ___ to Paris three times when I was a student.
preguntas.x: Para un número concreto de veces se usa past simple: I went three times. Used to y would expresan hábitos sin contar las veces (I used to go every summer), y el past continuous no sirve para hechos completos.

preguntas.q: I ___ like coffee, but now I can't start the day without it.
preguntas.x: La negación de used to es didn't use to + infinitivo. Wasn't used to significa «no estaba acostumbrado» y pide -ing, would no se usa con estados como like, y don't use to calca «no suelo».

preguntas.q: I've lived in London for a year, but I still can't get used to ___ on the left.
preguntas.x: En get used to y be used to, to es una preposición y va seguida de -ing: get used to driving. Drive es el error típico porque se confunde con used to + infinitivo.

preguntas.q: I ___ getting up early — I've done it for years, so it doesn't bother me at all.
preguntas.x: Be used to + -ing significa «estar acostumbrado»: I'm used to getting up early. Used to + verbo habla de un hábito pasado y no admite -ing, y get used to describe el proceso de acostumbrarse, que aquí ya terminó.

preguntas.q: When I met Carla, she ___ in London for six years, so she knew all the best places to eat.
preguntas.x: Una situación que ya duraba seis años en un momento del pasado (When I met Carla) va en past perfect continuous. Con for + duración hasta ese momento no sirven was living ni lived, y has been living llega hasta el presente.

preguntas.a: I was waiting for the bus when I saw the accident.
d: I waited for the bus while I was seeing the accident.
I was waiting for the bus while I saw the accident.
I was waiting for the bus when I was seeing the accident.
preguntas.x: La acción larga va en past continuous y la corta que la interrumpe en past simple, introducida por when. See describe aquí un hecho puntual, así que no va con while ni en continuo (was seeing).

preguntas.a: When I first met Ana, I didn't know she was Paolo's sister.
d: When I first met Ana, I wasn't knowing she was Paolo's sister.
When I first met Ana, I didn't know she had been Paolo's sister.
When I had first met Ana, I didn't know she was Paolo's sister.
preguntas.x: Know es un verbo de estado y no va en continuo, y ser hermana de alguien no es algo que terminara antes, así que no lleva past perfect. Tampoco hace falta en When I first met: los dos hechos ocurren a la vez.

preguntas.q: Choose the sentence that means the same as: “Working from home felt strange at first, but now it feels completely normal.”
preguntas.a: I've got used to working from home.
d: I used to work from home.
I'm used to work from home.
I've used to working from home.
preguntas.x: Get used to + -ing es el proceso de acostumbrarse, y en present perfect indica que ya lo logré. I used to work from home significa que antes lo hacía y ya no, y tras be used to hace falta -ing.

preguntas.q: She ___ three chapters of her thesis by the time the library closed.
preguntas.x: Con by the time y una cantidad terminada (three chapters) va past perfect simple. Had been writing destaca la actividad y no combina con un número de cosas acabadas, y ni was writing ni has written expresan que ya estaban hechos antes de ese momento pasado.

preguntas.q: It was the first time I ___ snow, so I took hundreds of photos.
preguntas.x: Con It was the first time va past perfect: It was the first time I had seen snow. Have seen solo sirve con It's the first time (presente), y see calca «era la primera vez que veía».

preguntas.q: Every Sunday, my grandad ___ us to the park and buy us an ice cream on the way home.
preguntas.x: Would + infinitivo expresa acciones repetidas en el pasado, y el segundo verbo sin to (buy) depende del mismo would. Con took haría falta bought; used to take también sería correcto, pero no está entre las opciones.

preguntas.q: Choose the sentence that means the same as: “We got to the cinema ten minutes after the film started.”
preguntas.a: When we got to the cinema, the film had been on for ten minutes.
d: When we got to the cinema, the film started ten minutes later.
The film had started ten minutes after we got to the cinema.
When we got to the cinema, the film was on for ten minutes.
preguntas.x: La película empezó antes de que llegáramos, así que va past perfect: the film had been on for ten minutes («llevaba diez minutos»). Was on for ten minutes no expresa duración hasta un momento pasado, y las otras dos opciones invierten el orden de los hechos.

preguntas.q: When she started her first job at eighteen, she had no idea that one day she ___ the whole company.
preguntas.x: Para lo que iba a ocurrir más tarde, visto desde un momento del pasado, se usa would (futuro en el pasado): she had no idea that one day she would run the company. Will no concuerda con un relato en pasado, y had run y used to run hablan de algo anterior o habitual.

preguntas.q: We ___ camping last weekend, but it rained so much that we stayed at home.
preguntas.x: Was/were going to expresa un plan del pasado que no se cumplió. Would go y used to go describen hábitos, no un plan concreto, y had gone diría que sí fuimos, lo que contradice we stayed at home.
